newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: St Francis eyes copper mining in Bolivia.
newsitem.headline: St Francis eyes copper mining in Bolivia.

text.p: Western Australia-based miner St Francis Mining NL said on Tuesday it is seeking to acquire up to 60 percent of the Chacarilla copper project in Bolivia.
St Francis Mining said it expects to complete a due diligence study of the project within two weeks with a view to negotiating a contract to take up a stake.

The project is now 60 percent-owned by Keswick International Investments Ltd, which is registered in the Bahamas, and 40 percent by Southern Shares Holding, registered in the Turks and Caicos Islands of the British West Indies.
The Chacarilla project consists of 17 contiguous concessions covering 7,500 hectares.
Copper has been mined in the Chacarilla district since the pre-Inca period, St Francis said.
Between 1966-1976, Japan's Nitto Metal Mining Co mined underground to yield most of the areas's recorded production.
About 1,457,000 tonnes of sulphide copper ore, grading 2.55 percent copper, was reportedly mined to produce a 50 percent copper concentrate at a recovery of 89 percent, the company said.
Mining was terminated in 1976 due to low copper prices, politics and labour disputes, St Francis said.
St Francis is exploring for nickel around Coolgardie, Western Australia.
